title: Conversational Throughput Profiles and Packaging Brief
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This brief defines a small set of conversational throughput profiles (usage archetypes) and maps each profile to recommended Redwood packaging, telemetry expectations, SLOs, and commercial guidance. The goal is to create a repeatable template sales/product can use when sizing customer commitments, designing default route configurations, and building telemetry dashboards in Console.

Context and problem statement

Teams building with Redwood receive a broad set of SLAs and deployment options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Despite this, we lack a short, prescriptive catalog that: (1) describes typical conversational workload shapes, (2) ties them to expected per-route performance (latency/throughput), and (3) maps to packaging SKUs and onboarding steps. This makes sizing and sales conversations lengthy and inconsistent.

Intended audience

- Product and pricing teams (commercialization)
- Solutions engineers and sales
- Runtime and platform engineers responsible for default policies and telemetry
- Customer success teams advising migration/onboarding

Profiles (definitions and signals)

We define four canonical profiles. Each profile has a short description, signal metrics observed in telemetry, and the recommended Redwood packaging SKU.

1) Interactive (low latency, low concurrency)
- Description: User-facing chat or assistant flows where a single request requires sub-200ms p95 response time and tight token latency. Typical for conversational UI with few parallel sessions per user.
- Signals: per-route p95 latency target <= 200ms; token throughput per session ~50-400 tokens; concurrency per tenant < 50 active sessions.
- Packaging: Hosted-Interactive (default hosted API), recommended default quantization: int8/awq where available.

2) Transactional High-Throughput (medium latency, high concurrency)
- Description: High-concurrency transactional endpoints (chatbots with many simultaneous users, search rerank pipelines) where throughput matters more than sub-100ms latency.
- Signals: p95 latency target 200-500ms; sustained concurrency 200-2,000 sessions; tokens/sec per route > 10k.
- Packaging: Dedicated Throughput pool with burst credits; enable continuous batching and KV prefix caching.

3) Batch/Analytics (high throughput, relaxed latency)
- Description: Bulk processing of messages or embeddings where latency can be minutes but cost per token is primary.
- Signals: asynchronous request queues, large batch sizes (> 1k items), latency SLOs measured in minutes/hours.
- Packaging: Dedicated (preemptible or spot-capacity) or Private with offline schedulers, suggested quantization: 4-bit / compressed kernels.

4) Edge/Local Light (ultra-low resource)
- Description: On-device or edge-proxied inference requiring small runtime memory and deterministic single-token latency.
- Signals: small sequence lengths, < 512 tokens, low memory footprint constraint, local-prefetch proxies enabled.
- Packaging: Private Edge runtime or embedded runtime SKUs; provide lightweight runtime binary and local cache coordinator.

Performance targets and SLOs (recommended defaults)

- Interactive (Hosted-Interactive): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 200ms, error rate <= 0.5%
- Transactional High-Throughput (Dedicated): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms, error rate <= 1%
- Batch/Analytics: completion within agreed time window (example: 95% of jobs within 30 minutes), job failure rate <= 2%
- Edge/Local Light: observed single-token latency <= 20ms on target hardware, memory usage < 4GB

Note: These are defaults. Sales and SRE should negotiate and convert into customer-specific SLOs.

Packaging recommendations (SKUs and feature toggles)

Each profile maps to a base SKU and one or more feature toggles. Use the following mapping when constructing quotes or default console templates: 

- Hosted-Interactive (SKU: hosted.interactive.v1)
  - Default features: streaming enabled, function-calling disabled by default, per-route token cap, prefix KV cache enabled for repeated prompts.
  - Autoscaler policy: conservative (scale on p95 latency breach), burst credits: 0.

- Dedicated-Throughput (SKU: dedicated.throughput.standard)
  - Default features: continuous batching enabled, high-concurrency routing, adaptive quantization suggestions enabled via Optimize.
  - Autoscaler policy: aggressive (scale on queue depth), burst credits: configurable (recommended 10% of capacity).

- Dedicated-BatchSpot (SKU: dedicated.batch.spot)
  - Default features: offline scheduler, preemptible instance support, bulk-API endpoint (bulk/v1).
  - Autoscaler policy: scheduled windows + opportunistic scaling.

- Private-Edge (SKU: private.edge.light)
  - Default features: local-prefetch proxy, compact runtime binary, simplified observability capture.

Pricing guidance (high-level heuristics)

The intent is to provide consistent ways to translate observed telemetry into SKU suggestions and high level pricing conversation points: 

1) Map concurrency to required GPU hours per day using empirical conversion: estimated GPU-hours/day = (mean_tokens_per_day / tokens_per_gpu_hour_lookup[model_variant]). Maintain an internal lookup table (owned by the Pricing team) that maps common model variants to tokens/hr for typical instance types.

2) For Hosted-Interactive: price on per-token with tiered discounts at 1M, 10M, 100M tokens per month. Offer a warm-capacity subscription add-on for high SLO guarantees.

3) For Dedicated: use committed monthly capacity with baseline reserved GPU-hours and burst credits. Include a per-route throughput uplift surcharge for continuous batching and guaranteed p95.

4) BatchSpot: discount of 40–70% relative to dedicated baseline depending on preemptibility and retention guarantees.

Rollout and onboarding playbook (6-step canonical flow)

1) Discovery and telemetry pull (SE + CSM)
   - Request 7 days of traffic trace or synthetic capture from customer (format: ndjson events with route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms).
   - Run the 'redwood-sim' workload estimator (see Appendix).
2) Profile assignment and SKU recommendation (Product + Pricing)
   - Use the rulebook: if peak concurrency > 200 AND tokens/sec > 5k => Dedicated-Throughput recommended.
3) PoC config and route templates (Engineering)
   - Provide route template: streaming=true, batch_window_ms=30, kv_prefix_cache=true for Dedicated-Throughput.
4) Trial and metrics baseline (CSM + SRE)
   - Run 72-hour pilot on a mirrored traffic slice, monitor p95 and token cost.
5) Commercial negotiation and contract (Sales + Finance)
   - Propose reserved capacity+burst credits or hosted tiers with warm-capacity add-on depending on risk tolerance.
6) Production cutover and Ops runbook handoff (SRE)
   - Provide runbook: escalation steps, fallback to model-variant v2, circuit-breaker thresholds.

Implementation details (templates and examples)

Example route JSON (suggested default for Dedicated-Throughput):

{
  "route_name": "customer-chat-main",
  "runtime": "redwood-runtime-v3",
  "model_variant": "open-llama-70b-int8",
  "streaming": true,
  "batching": {
    "mode": "continuous",
    "max_batch_ms": 30,
    "max_batch_tokens": 4096
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "enabled": true,
    "prefix_ttl_seconds": 600
  },
  "fidelity_settings": {
    "quant_profile": "recommended-by-optimize",
    "fallback_variant": "open-llama-70b-pt-8"
  }
}

CLI commands for load simulation (internal tooling):

# run a 10-minute synthetic burst sim
redwood-sim run --route customer-chat-main --duration 600 --concurrency 500 --pattern poisson --model open-llama-70b-int8

Telemetry and observability expectations

For every profile, Console should surface the following per-route dashboards by default:
- Token consumption (tokens in/out, per-minute)
- Latency histogram (p50/p95/p99)
- Batch sizes and batch latency distribution
- KV cache hit rate and prefix eviction rate
- Cost-per-1000-tokens estimate (derived)

Alerting defaults (recommended)

- p95 latency breach for 10 consecutive minutes => severity P2 alert to SRE (owner: eng-sre/runtime-team)
- Error rate spike > 2x baseline for 5 minutes => P1 incident playbook can be engaged
- Token consumption exceeds committed capacity by 20% in 1-hour window => notify sales/finance for crediting adjustments

Ownership and decision points

- Product: final SKU naming, commercial packaging terms, and the copied guidance in the quoting tool.
- Engineering (serving-runtime): implement the route templates and ensure runtime honors batch_window_ms and kv_prefix_ttl.
- Eng-SRE: create default alerts/dashboards and own the pilot runbook.
- Pricing/Finance: maintain tokens_per_gpu_hour_lookup table and discount rules.

Appendix: redwood-sim estimator (algorithm summary)

redwood-sim runs a 3-stage estimation: (1) aggregate token trace to derive tokens/sec and concurrency distribution, (2) map tokens/sec to model-variant GPU throughput using tokens_per_gpu_hour_lookup, (3) apply overhead multipliers for continuous batching (0.9–1.2) and replication (1.0–1.5) to produce recommended GPU-hours/day.

Example table (text)

| Profile | p95 latency target | Suggested SKU | Key toggles | Typical discount |
|--------|--------------------|---------------|-------------|------------------|
| Interactive | <=200ms | hosted.interactive.v1 | streaming, kv_cache | 0-10% |
| Transactional | 200-500ms | dedicated.throughput.standard | batching, burst credits | 5-25% |
| Batch/Analytics | minutes | dedicated.batch.spot | offline scheduler, preemptible | 40-70% |
| Edge/Local | single-token <20ms | private.edge.light | local-prefetch, compact runtime | N/A |

Appendix: example telemetry snapshot (ndjson line example)

{
  "timestamp": "2026-09-01T12:03:21Z",
  "route": "customer-chat-main",
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "tokens_in": 128,
  "tokens_out": 280,
  "latency_ms": 142
}

Open questions and follow-ups

- Should we add a pre-flight API that automatically returns a recommended SKU based on a 7-day trace upload? (Product/Engineering)
- What is the acceptance boundary for Recommend-by-Optimize quant profiles in Dedicated vs Hosted? (Optimization team)
- Decide on the exact discount cadence for multi-month committed dedicated pools (Pricing/Finance)
